provenance: Human-authored from standard stream-processing / event-log curriculum (logs, Kafka-style brokers, windowing, exactly-once). Not derived from Synapse gold JSONL.
review_notes: Focused inventory for stream processing architectures; includes Kafka as a named technology commonly taught in this curriculum.

concepts.title: Event Logs
concepts.description: Append-only ordered records of events used as a system of record.

concepts.title: Kafka
concepts.description: Distributed event streaming platform organized around topics, partitions, and consumer groups.

concepts.title: Topics and Partitions
concepts.description: Logical streams split into ordered partitions for scale and parallelism.

concepts.title: Consumer Groups
concepts.description: Coordinated sets of consumers that share partition assignment for a topic.

concepts.title: Windowing
concepts.description: Grouping unbounded streams into finite time or count windows for aggregation.

concepts.title: Watermarks
concepts.description: Progress markers estimating event-time completeness in out-of-order streams.

concepts.title: Exactly-Once
concepts.description: Processing semantics that avoid lost or duplicated effects under retries.

concepts.title: Stream Processing
concepts.description: Continuous computation over unbounded event streams.

concepts.title: Stateful Stream Processing
concepts.description: Maintaining keyed state while processing streams, including recovery concerns.
